---
title: "Combine Glyco Summary Files into a Matrix"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load necessary library
library(dplyr)

# List all text files in the working directory
files <- list.files(pattern = "\\.txt$")

# Function to process each file
process_file <- function(file) {
  # Read the file, skipping the first 3 rows (so data start with row 4)
  df <- read.delim(file, header = TRUE, skip = 3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  
  # Rename the first column (Column A) to "Scan/Ion"
  names(df)[1] <- "Scan/Ion"
  
  # Extract the first 10 characters of the file name to use as a prefix
  prefix <- substr(basename(file), 1, 15)
  
  # Identify the "Total" and "%Total" columns and rename them by adding the prefix.
  # (Adjust case if needed; here we assume the headers are exactly "Total" and "%Total")
  current_names <- names(df)
  idx_total <- which(current_names == "Total")
  idx_pctTotal <- which(current_names == "%Total")
  
  new_total <- paste0(prefix, "_Total")
  new_pctTotal <- paste0(prefix, "_%Total")
  
  if(length(idx_total) == 1) {
    names(df)[idx_total] <- new_total
  }
  if(length(idx_pctTotal) == 1) {
    names(df)[idx_pctTotal] <- new_pctTotal
  }
  
  # Select only the columns of interest: "Scan/Ion", and the newly renamed total columns.
  df_subset <- df[, c("Scan/Ion", new_total, new_pctTotal)]
  return(df_subset)
}

# Process each file and store the results in a list
data_list <- lapply(files, process_file)

# Merge all data frames by the "Scan/Ion" column
combined_df <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "Scan/Ion", all = TRUE), data_list)

# Convert the combined data frame to a matrix:
# Use the "Scan/Ion" column as row names and remove it from the matrix.
combined_matrix <- as.matrix(combined_df[,-1])
rownames(combined_matrix) <- combined_df$`Scan/Ion`

# Display the resulting matrix
combined_matrix
```


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# A helper function to trim whitespace
trim <- function(x) {
  gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$", "", x)
}

# Function to process one file
process_file <- function(file) {
  # Read the entire file as lines and skip the first 3 lines (cells A1–A3)
  lines <- readLines(file)
  if(length(lines) <= 3) stop("File has too few lines!")
  lines <- lines[-(1:3)]
  
  # The very first line (A4) is assumed to be the header row.
  header_line <- lines[1]
  header_fields <- unlist(strsplit(header_line, "\t"))
  # Force the first header to be "Scan/Ion"
  header_fields[1] <- "Scan/Ion"
  
  # List to collect processed rows; first row will be the header (we keep it as is)
  processed_rows <- list(header_fields)
  
  # Initialize current group as NA
  current_group <- NA
  
  # Process each subsequent line (preserving order)
  for(i in 2:length(lines)) {
    line <- lines[i]
    
    # Check if this is a group header line: it starts with backslashes.
    if(grepl("^\\\\+", line)) {
      # Remove all backslashes and trim; if any text remains, treat it as the group name.
      grp <- trim(gsub("\\\\", "", line))
      if(nchar(grp) > 0) {
        current_group <- grp
      }
      # Do not add the group header line itself to the data.
      next
    }
    
    # (Optional) Skip repeated header rows (if the line equals the header_line after trimming)
    if(trim(line) == trim(header_line)) next
    
    # Split the line into fields by tab
    fields <- unlist(strsplit(line, "\t"))
    # If there are too few fields, skip the line.
    if(length(fields) < 3) next
    
    # For data rows (i.e. not the overall header), if a current group is set,
    # prepend the group name to the first field (unless it already contains it).
    if(!is.na(current_group)) {
      if(!grepl(current_group, fields[1], ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        fields[1] <- paste(current_group, fields[1], sep=": ")
      }
    }
    
    processed_rows[[length(processed_rows) + 1]] <- fields
  }
  
  # To ensure every row has the same number of columns, pad shorter rows with NA.
  max_cols <- max(sapply(processed_rows, length))
  processed_rows <- lapply(processed_rows, function(x) { length(x) <- max_cols; x })
  
  # Convert list of rows into a data frame.
  df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, processed_rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  # Use the first row as header names and remove it from data.
  colnames(df) <- df[1, ]
  df <- df[-1, ]
  
  # Keep only the columns "Scan/Ion", "Total" and "%Total"
  # (Assumes these column names appear exactly; adjust if needed.)
  cols_to_keep <- c("Scan/Ion", "Total", "%Total")
  df <- df[, cols_to_keep, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Extract a file prefix (first 7 characters of the file name)
  prefix <- substr(basename(file), 1, 10)
  
  # Rename the "Total" and "%Total" columns by prefixing them
  colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "Total"] <- paste0(prefix, "_Total")
  colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "%Total"] <- paste0(prefix, "_%Total")
  
  return(df)
}

# List all text files (adjust pattern as needed)
files <- list.files(pattern = "\\.txt$")

# Process each file and store results in a list
data_list <- lapply(files, process_file)

# Combine data from multiple files.
# This code assumes that the "Scan/Ion" column (first column) is identical and in the same order.
if(length(data_list) > 0) {
  combined_df <- data_list[[1]]
  if(length(data_list) > 1) {
    for(i in 2:length(data_list)) {
      if(!all(combined_df$`Scan/Ion` == data_list[[i]]$`Scan/Ion`)) {
        stop("The 'Scan/Ion' values do not match across files!")
      }
      # Append the numeric columns (drop the "Scan/Ion" column from subsequent files)
      combined_df <- cbind(combined_df, data_list[[i]][, -1, drop = FALSE])
    }
  }
  
  # Convert the combined data (excluding "Scan/Ion") to a matrix,
  # using "Scan/Ion" as the row names.
  combined_matrix <- as.matrix(combined_df[, -1, drop = FALSE])
  rownames(combined_matrix) <- combined_df$`Scan/Ion`
  
  # Display the resulting matrix
  combined_matrix
}
```


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# A helper function to trim whitespace
trim <- function(x) {
  gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$", "", x)
}

# Function to process one file
process_file <- function(file) {
  # Read all lines from the file and skip the first 3 lines
  lines <- readLines(file)
  if(length(lines) <= 3) stop("File has too few lines!")
  lines <- lines[-(1:3)]
  
  # The first line (A4) is assumed to be the header row.
  header_line <- lines[1]
  header_fields <- unlist(strsplit(header_line, "\t"))
  # Rename the first header to "Scan/Ion"
  header_fields[1] <- "Scan/Ion"
  
  # List to store processed rows (first row is header)
  processed_rows <- list(header_fields)
  
  # Initialize current group as NA
  current_group <- NA
  
  # Process each subsequent line (preserving order)
  for(i in 2:length(lines)) {
    line <- lines[i]
    
    # Check for group header rows (starting with backslashes)
    if(grepl("^\\\\+", line)) {
      # Remove backslashes and trim to obtain group name (e.g., "HexNAc")
      grp <- trim(gsub("\\\\", "", line))
      if(nchar(grp) > 0) {
        current_group <- grp
      }
      # Do not add the group header line to data rows
      next
    }
    
    # (Optional) Skip repeated header rows
    if(trim(line) == trim(header_line)) next
    
    # Split the line into fields using tab as delimiter
    fields <- unlist(strsplit(line, "\t"))
    # Skip if there are too few fields
    if(length(fields) < 3) next
    
    # Prepend the group name (if available) to the first field, unless already present
    if(!is.na(current_group)) {
      if(!grepl(current_group, fields[1], ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        fields[1] <- paste(current_group, fields[1], sep=": ")
      }
    }
    
    processed_rows[[length(processed_rows) + 1]] <- fields
  }
  
  # Pad rows to have the same number of columns
  max_cols <- max(sapply(processed_rows, length))
  processed_rows <- lapply(processed_rows, function(x) { length(x) <- max_cols; x })
  
  # Convert the list of rows into a data frame
  df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, processed_rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  # Use the first row as column names, then remove it from the data
  colnames(df) <- df[1, ]
  df <- df[-1, ]
  
  # Keep only the columns "Scan/Ion", "Total", and "%Total"
  cols_to_keep <- c("Scan/Ion", "Total", "%Total")
  df <- df[, cols_to_keep, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Extract the file prefix (first 10 characters of the file name)
  prefix <- substr(basename(file), 1, 15)
  
  # Rename the "Total" and "%Total" columns by adding the prefix
  colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "Total"] <- paste0(prefix, "_Total")
  colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "%Total"] <- paste0(prefix, "_%Total")
  
  return(df)
}

# List all text files (adjust the pattern if needed)
files <- list.files(pattern = "\\.txt$")

# Process each file and store the results in a list
data_list <- lapply(files, process_file)

# Combine the data frames assuming that the "Scan/Ion" column is identical and in the same order.
if(length(data_list) > 0) {
  combined_df <- data_list[[1]]
  if(length(data_list) > 1) {
    for(i in 2:length(data_list)) {
      if(!all(combined_df$`Scan/Ion` == data_list[[i]]$`Scan/Ion`)) {
        stop("The 'Scan/Ion' values do not match across files!")
      }
      # Append the numeric columns (excluding "Scan/Ion") from each subsequent file
      combined_df <- cbind(combined_df, data_list[[i]][, -1, drop = FALSE])
    }
  }
  
  ## Group the numeric columns:
  # Extract column names corresponding to the "Total" and "%Total" values
  total_cols <- grep("_Total$", colnames(combined_df), value = TRUE)
  pcttotal_cols <- grep("_%Total$", colnames(combined_df), value = TRUE)
  
  # Reorder columns so that the first column remains "Scan/Ion",
  # then all "Total" columns, followed by all "%Total" columns.
  combined_df <- combined_df[, c("Scan/Ion", total_cols, pcttotal_cols)]
  
  # Convert the numeric portion of the data frame into a matrix.
  # Row names will be the "Scan/Ion" column.
  combined_matrix <- as.matrix(combined_df[, -1, drop = FALSE])
  rownames(combined_matrix) <- combined_df$`Scan/Ion`
  
  # Display the combined data frame and the matrix.
  print("Combined Data Frame:")
  print(combined_df)
  
  print("Combined Matrix (numeric columns only):")
  print(combined_matrix)
}

write.csv(combined_df, "combined_Glycounter_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
